scope: the deployed staging site (one manual rate-limit test)

tools.name: semgrep 1.180.0
tools.config: p/python p/javascript p/typescript p/react p/dockerfile p/github-actions p/secrets (run-semgrep.sh)

tools.name: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code)
tools.config: read auth.py, main.py, Dockerfile, deploy/, Caddyfile, mcp-server/, .claude/; prompts in audit-brief.md

tools.name: curl against staging
tools.config: 7 wrong-password logins, each with a different spoofed X-Forwarded-For

findings.title: Third-party actions referenced by mutable tags
findings.evidence: Every `uses:` pointed at a tag (`@v7`, `@v4`, ...). The deploy jobs hold `id-token: write` (they assume the AWS deploy role) and the build job holds `packages: write`, so a moved tag would run someone else's code with those permissions.
findings.rationale: Cheap to fix, and the jobs that use these actions can deploy to production.
findings.fix: Pinned all 7 actions to full commit SHAs with the version as a comment; added .github/dependabot.yml so the pins (and the npm/uv lockfiles) get weekly update PRs.

findings.title: curl output piped onward in a run step
findings.evidence: Read each step. The smoke test pipes to `grep -q` and to a fixed `python3 -c` JSON assertion against the app it just built; the OIDC steps pipe GitHub's own token endpoint into a fixed `python3 -c` that prints five claims. Nothing downloaded is executed as a script.
findings.rationale: The rule matches any `curl ... |`; it cannot tell a parser from a shell.
findings.fix: Annotated each `run:` with `nosemgrep: <rule> -- <reason>` so CI stays green without disabling the rule.

findings.title: Workflow input expanded directly into a shell script
findings.evidence: `${{ inputs.environment == 'production' && 'prod' || 'staging' }}` was spliced into the script. The input is a `choice` (staging|production) and the expression only yields the two literals, so it was not exploitable; only repo writers can dispatch the workflow.
findings.rationale: Not exploitable today, but the pattern is the one that becomes exploitable when someone later changes the input to free text.
findings.fix: The input now reaches the shell as env var TARGET_ENV, mapped with a `case` that rejects anything else.

findings.title: source-map-js 1.2.1: event-loop denial of service via crafted source maps
findings.evidence: Fixed in 1.2.2. It runs only during `npm run build` on our own sources; it is not in the shipped bundle or the runtime image.
findings.rationale: Build-time only, so low in context, but the fix is a patch bump of a lockfile entry.

findings.title: Secrets hook did not cover the Compose .env or the server env files
findings.evidence: The project hook blocked only `backend/.env` and `backend/card_catalog.db`. The Compose `.env` next to docker-compose.yml holds AUTH_* and POSTGRES_PASSWORD, and /srv/card-catalog/prod.env and staging.env (RDS URL, AUTH_*) are on the same host as this checkout. Tested the widened hook with 8 paths: all 5 secret/data paths exit 2, `.env.example` files and README exit 0.
findings.rationale: This is the one guardrail that is enforced outside the model; it should cover every secrets file an agent on this host can reach.
findings.fix: Blocked suffixes are now `/.env`, `/prod.env`, `/staging.env`, `backend/card_catalog.db`; docs/permissions.md updated. Bash writes are still not covered (see capability-table.md).

findings.title: Uvicorn trusts X-Forwarded-For from any address; the login rate limiter keys on it
findings.evidence: Manual test against staging: 7 wrong logins, each with a different spoofed X-Forwarded-For, returned 401 x5 then 429 x2. Caddy replaces client-supplied X-Forwarded-* from untrusted clients, and the app containers publish no ports on the server.
findings.rationale: Not exploitable in the deployed topology. It becomes exploitable if the app is ever exposed without Caddy, or Caddy is configured with trusted_proxies.

findings.title: Existing sessions survive a password change and logout
findings.evidence: Sessions are stateless signed tokens valid for 30 days. Logout only deletes the browser's cookie; set-password.sh changes AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH but not AUTH_SECRET_KEY, so a stolen cookie keeps working after the password is reset.
findings.rationale: Owner approved on 2026-10-21: a password reset should end every session.
findings.fix: deploy/set-password.sh now also writes a new random AUTH_SECRET_KEY (openssl rand -hex 32, different per environment) before restarting the containers. Tested on scratch env files: one hash and one key per file, other lines kept, keys differ between prod and staging, hash verifies; mismatch and short passwords change nothing. The same change fixed the prompt echoing the password (getpass inside `docker run -i` can't disable echo; the script now turns echo off on the host terminal).

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy or frame protection on the site
findings.evidence: Response headers include HSTS, nosniff and Referrer-Policy, but no CSP or X-Frame-Options, so the board can be framed by another site (clickjacking). React escapes output and the frontend has no innerHTML/eval sinks (grep), which limits XSS impact.
findings.rationale: Proposed fix: `X-Frame-Options DENY` and a CSP with `frame-ancestors 'none'` in the common Caddy snippet. Needs a Caddy reload on the server and a check that the Vite build works under the CSP.

findings.title: Container base images referenced by mutable tags
findings.evidence: Same class as F01 for images. The app image itself is deployed by commit SHA, so a release is reproducible once built; the base images are resolved at build time.
findings.rationale: Pinning by digest needs Dependabot's docker ecosystem to stay current; worth doing together with F08's Caddy change.

findings.title: Deploy jobs still run the OIDC-claims debug step
findings.evidence: The step requests an ID token and prints only sub/aud/iss/environment/ref, never the token. It was added to diagnose the trust-policy mismatch, which is fixed.
findings.rationale: Kept on purpose: it is the fastest way to diagnose the next trust-policy failure (docs/deployment.md). Remove it if the deploy jobs ever need to be minimal.

findings.title: /docs and /openapi.json are public
findings.evidence: https://cards.terzotech.net/docs returns 200. Every card route still requires a session; the same contract is in the public repo as openapi.yaml.
findings.rationale: Reveals nothing that is not already public, and it is useful to reviewers.

findings.title: Rate limiter never forgets an IP it has seen
findings.evidence: Keys are pruned lazily per IP but never evicted, so memory grows with the number of distinct client addresses that fail a login. Bounded in practice by one small app behind Caddy.
findings.rationale: Documented single-instance limit (README); a restart clears it.
